correctness.rationale: For each length n>=1, height-one excursions are indexed bijectively by all even-cardinality subsets of [n]. The published alternating-interval criterion excludes all differing intervals except adjacent flat/nonflat swaps, which precisely move one token on P_n. In each even-token layer the first-mixed-(2i-1,2i) edge involution leaves C(floor(n/2),t) unmatched vertices all on the parity-t side; the matching bound and parity coloring coincide, proving capacity. Independent edge-boundary enumeration, sorted-coordinate distance proof, and Young-tableau geodesic proof establish remaining claims. Standalone verify.py ran exact deletion-set equality through n=10 and matching formula through n=18; distance_check.py ran independent exhaustive BFS through n=9. Finite computation is validation only, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact characterization of a constrained single-deletion two-read communication channel by the path-token graph yields constructive maximum zero-error codebooks for every length and arch count, plus connected confusability strata, exact edge complexity, distances, and shortest ambiguity chains. Motivated by synchronization/reconstruction of a natural height-limited path language, it is not an arbitrary finite slice or known numerical table alone. The general token-graph alpha and tableau facts are antecedents, but the correspondence creates a reusable design principle; no claim is made about height>=2 or one-read deletion correction.
